analysis.analysis: 'The Provenance: Journal of Forensic Semiotics is an academic publication exploring the intersection of sign theory, digital authorship, and criminology. It centers on the analysis of how traces, texts, and synthetic media carry (or fabricate) verifiable lineage, meaning, and authenticity in legal and investigative contexts' (cites Academia.edu +4). Expanded: 'Recent literature in or referencing the journal focuses on three core areas: AI & Document Authenticity — Explores semiotic disruptions caused by AI-generated deepfakes. It examines how synthetic documents mimic authentic representamina (signs), requiring indexical stress tests and cryptographic provenance anchoring' (ResearchGate); 'Process Provenance — Introduces the concept of process provenance as the structural mechanism separating authentic authorship from generative slop, establishing verifiable lineage in human-machine collaborative writing.'
